metadata.title: Density Pass 27 -- Iverson's Pits (Ticks 50-60)
metadata.description: One of the most devastating single-brigade actions of the entire war. Iverson's North Carolina brigade advances without skirmishers, walks into an ambush behind a stone wall, and loses 900 of 1400 men in minutes. Iverson reportedly breaks down. The survivors surrender en masse -- the largest single-unit surrender in the battle. A story almost never told in detail.

placements.notes: 5th NC -- Iverson's lead regiment. No skirmishers deployed. Iverson watches from the rear.
23rd NC -- the flank regiment, about to be hit hardest
Paul's brigade behind the stone wall on Oak Ridge -- 1200 rifles leveled at Iverson's exposed flank
Baxter's brigade in position -- they have been waiting
5th NC IN THE PITS -- 290 of 470 down in the first volley. The survivors fall into a depression and surrender.
12th NC -- 139 of 219 killed or wounded in minutes. 80 survivors.
20th NC devastated -- 232 casualties from one volley. Lying in ranks in the wheat field.
23rd NC -- worst of all. 226 of 316 down. The regiment is destroyed as a fighting unit.
Paul's brigade pursuing -- sweeping forward to collect prisoners from the stunned Confederates
Baxter's brigade -- over 500 Confederates surrender in the wheat field
5th NC survivors -- those who didn't surrender fleeing west
23rd NC -- 60 men from 316. Iverson reportedly weeping, unable to command.
Ramseur's brigade coming up -- trying to restore the collapsed Confederate line on Oak Ridge
Paul's brigade with 500+ prisoners -- one of the most complete destructions of a brigade in the war
12th NC survivors -- Iverson's brigade has lost 900 of 1400 men in 20 minutes
